piles.label: Thranduil's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Thranduil's Elves-and-graveyard deck better. Thranduil borrows the activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard and loots whenever a legendary Elf enters, so a non-Elf card has to beat an Elf for its slot.

piles.label: Glarb's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Glarb's draw-to-mill deck better. Every draw mills the opponent, Bruvac and The Water Crystal multiply it, and Glarb casts mana value 4+ straight off the top.

piles.label: Either deck
piles.intro: Cards that work in both decks: shared removal, ramp and fixing, scry Elves, planeswalkers. Copies are shared in Arena, so one card can sit in both lists.

piles.label: Fits neither
piles.intro: Cards that fit neither deck, each with the reason. Listed so nothing is silently dropped.

Legolas, Counter of Kills.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf body; minor text. **Glarb:** Minor.

Tam, Observant Sequencer // Deep Sight.text: Owned. Draw one on landfall-prepared casts; small.

Elrond, Master of Healing.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; counters on scry, draws when targeted. **Glarb:** Few creatures to put counters on.

Ezuri, Stalker of Spheres.text: "Whenever you proliferate, draw a card" — the deck has one proliferate source (Vraska, Betrayal's Sting).

Jyoti, Moag Ancient.text: Needs commander recasts and land creatures.

Kiora, the Crashing Wave.text: **Thranduil:** −1 draw + extra land; +1 fogs one threat. **Glarb:** Same.

Nael, Avizoa Aeronaut.text: Domain: Sultai lands give at most 3 basic types, so "if there are five … draw a card" never happens.

Rashmi, Eternities Crafter.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; a free spell off the top each turn. Bench in both. **Glarb:** Same, and the top card is visible under Glarb, so you know when it hits.

Imoti, Celebrant of Bounty.text: Cascade on mana value 6+ — the deck has few 6+ spells.

Kruphix, God of Horizons.text: Hand-size enabler only; rarely a creature in three colours.

Tamiyo, Compleated Sage.text: "−X: Exile target nonland permanent card with mana value X from your graveyard" — Same; the +1 tap is tempo, not removal.

Tawnos, the Toymaker.text: Copies Beasts/Birds; neither deck has them.

Oko, the Trickster.text: Six mana for counters; weak here.

Bonny Pall, Clearcutter.text: 6 mana; "Whenever you attack, draw a card, then … put a land card from your hand or graveyard onto the battlefield" — real value, wrong curve slot beside Selvala/Kamahl's Vow.

Tishana, Voice of Thunder.text: Draws one per creature you control — usually 2–4 here; 7 mana.

Kotis, Sibsig Champion.text: "cast a creature spell from your graveyard by exiling three other cards from your graveyard" — Three cards a turn, in a yard that is mostly Elves; Muldrotha recasts without exiling anything.

Leovold, Emissary of Trest.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** "Each opponent can't draw more than one card each turn" switches off Dictate of Kruphix and Seizan's extra draws for them — it fights this deck's mill.

Nashi, Moon's Legacy.text: "exile up to one target legendary or Rat card from your graveyard and copy it" — Can target a non-Elf legend, but the deck's legends ARE mostly Elves; menace 3-drop otherwise.

Nashi, Illusion Gadgeteer.text: Conjures a copy of a yard card into hand (keeps the original — no G-42 cost); a 4-mana non-Elf. ◇

Kotis, the Fangkeeper.text: Exiles X on combat damage and casts them free — an aggressive card in a deck that wins by milling.

Sidisi, Brood Tyrant.text: Not an Elf, and its mill is random where Thranduil's loot chooses — Mills three on entry and attack; with 45 creatures most mills make a 2/2 Zombie. Strong, just not Elf-synergistic (the Zombies feed nothing Elf-gated).

Gonti, Canny Acquisitor.text: Steals a card on combat damage; the deck is a control deck that rarely connects.

Brokkos, Apex of Forever.text: Recursive mutate threat; Elves are non-Human so it can mutate, but it adds a body, not an engine.

Maralen, Fae Ascendant.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** Exiles two of their library per Elf or Faerie entering — this deck has almost none.

Yarok, the Desecrated.text: **Thranduil:** If a permanent entering causes a trigger "that ability triggers an additional time" — Thranduil's legendary-Elf loot becomes draw 4, discard 2, and every Elf ETB doubles. **Strong add.** **Glarb:** Doubles Sphinx Mindbreaker (mill 20) and Sheoldred's edict, but few ETBs here.

Sin, Spira's Punishment.text: "exile a permanent card from your graveyard at random" — Random — will hit Elves; 7 mana.

Mimeoplasm, Revered One.text: "exile up to X creature cards from your graveyard" — Eats exactly the Elf creature cards Thranduil borrows from.

Glamdring, Foe-hammer // Gleam of Death.text: An Equipment for an instants deck.

Fblthp, Impossibly Lost.text: **Thranduil:** Draw two on combat damage. **Glarb:** Rarely attacks.

Jace Reawakened.text: **Thranduil:** Loot every turn — feeds the yard. **Glarb:** Loot draws mill two.

Marit Lage's Slumber.text: Needs snow permanents; neither deck has any.

Mystic Reflection.text: Copies a nonlegendary creature; same problem as Mindlink Mech.

Malcolm, Alluring Scoundrel.text: Combat-gated loot on a non-Elf flier.

Naban, Dean of Iteration.text: Doubles Wizard ETBs; neither deck is Wizards.

Proft's Eidetic Memory.text: Draws one, no hand size, counters on combat — the counters do nothing here.

Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari.text: Loot that untaps on legendary spells — the closest of the looters, since most of the deck is legendary.

The Key to the Vault.text: Equipment that casts from YOUR library on combat damage — combat-gated.

Vnwxt, Verbose Host.text: Speed needs opponent life loss; slow in both.

Arni, Humble Scribe.text: `{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card` duplicates Thranduil's own loot; lost to an Elf.

Chandra, Chill of Compliance.text: Owned. +1 surveil feeds Matoya and Proft; the other +1 adds mana for noncreature spells; −X stuns a threat. Screened KEY against the list.

Callaphe, Beloved of the Sea.text: A mild ward tax; no engine.

Elrond, Lord of Rivendell.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; scry 1 per creature entering — modest. **Glarb:** Each scry triggers Matoya — a draw per creature entering. Close.

Elrond, Moon-Reader.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** "Whenever you activate an ability of a creature, draw a card" (once a turn) — Glarb's own surveil tap triggers it, so every turn is a draw that mills two. **Good add here too.**

Fblthp, Lost on the Range.text: Plots from the top — a slower version of what Glarb already does.

Geralf, the Fleshwright.text: Needs several cheap spells a turn.

Graviton, Fundamental Force.text: Draw-trigger tapper — minor in Glarb's deck.

Impossible Man.text: Clone utility without a target worth copying every turn.

Ioreth of the Healing House.text: **Thranduil:** `{T}: Untap two other target legendary creatures` — untap Thranduil for a second borrowed {T} ability each turn (Dionus's job, again). **Strong add.** **Glarb:** Untaps Glarb for a second surveil 2, which Matoya turns into a second draw. Real, smaller.

Katara, Bending Prodigy.text: A weak body for either deck.

Kira, Great Glass-Spinner.text: Counters the first targeting of each creature — including your own pump or untap (Ioreth, Dionus).

Lyra, Tolarian Archangel.text: Owned. A 3/3 Angel at end step when you drew three — common here, but it is a body, not a draw or a mill.

Mindlink Mech.text: Copies a nonlegendary creature; both decks are mostly legends.

Unctus, Grand Metatect.text: Rummage on blue artifact creatures; few here.

Alora, Rogue Companion.text: Evasion that returns the creature to hand — tempo only.

Arwen's Gift.text: Scry 2, draw 2 (cheaper with two legends); one-shot.

Charix, the Raging Isle.text: Counts Islands; three-colour decks run only a few.

Gale, Conduit of the Arcane.text: Pays off instants/sorceries; Thranduil runs 8, and Glarb's 21 already have better payoffs.

God-Eternal Kefnet.text: Copies instants/sorceries drawn — Glarb sees the top, but Kefnet wants them first-drawn each turn; minor.

Gandalf, Friend of the Shire.text: Ring-tempt payoff; neither deck tempts the Ring.

Irenicus's Vile Duplication.text: Clones a legend — strong only with one ETB engine to copy.

Jace, the Perfected Mind.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** −X mills yourself 3X — self-mill on demand; `{2}{U}{U/P}`.

Jace, Wielder of Mysteries.text: +1 mills two and draws one (four milled under Corrosion); its alt-win needs YOUR library empty, which this deck never aims for. `{1}{U}{U}{U}` is hard in three colours.

Leader, Super-Genius.text: Connive each combat; duplicates Thranduil's loot on a non-Elf body.

Multiversal Recruitment.text: **Thranduil:** Copy Priest of Titania or Voice of the Woods, flashback later. Fine. **Glarb:** "Create a token that's a copy of target creature you control, except it isn't legendary" — a second Bruvac quadruples every mill. **Spicy add.**

Orvar, the All-Form.text: Needs instants that target your own permanents.

Taeko, the Patient Avalanche.text: A blink/bounce payoff; no blink in either deck.

The Clone Saga.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 3 fills the yard; II copies a creature spell. **Glarb:** Surveil 3 triggers Matoya and Proft.

Tui and La, Moon and Ocean.text: An attacker draw engine; neither deck attacks enough.

Vesuvan Duplimancy.text: Needs spells that target your creatures.

Yue, the Moon Spirit.text: A noncreature-spells payoff; both decks are creature-heavy or draw-heavy.

Jace, Memory Adept.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** Its 0 "Target player mills ten cards" can target YOU — ten cards of Elves for Thranduil. **Good add here too.**

Jace, Unraveler of Secrets.text: 5 mana; +1 scry 1 then draw (Matoya draws again). Close; −2 bounce is tempo.

Krang, the All-Powerful.text: "If a player drawing a card causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time" doubles Psychic Corrosion, both Tutelages, Sheoldred and The Theorist — the deck's whole engine. **Strongest add on this list.** Left out on slot count.

Pharaoh Rama-Tut.text: Connives on noncreature spells — 19 here; a non-Elf looter.

Syr Elenora, the Discerning.text: A hand-size body; Glarb's deck has better.

Thryx, the Sudden Storm.text: Spells with mana value 5+ cost {1} less and can't be countered — a flash flier; the deck's MV 5+ spells mostly come off the top already.

Kitsune, Dragon's Daughter.text: **Thranduil:** 6 mana: swap a weak creature of yours for their best. **Glarb:** Same; mana value 6, so Glarb can cast it off the top.

Pol Jamaar, Illusionist.text: Missed by the pile pass. "Choose a creature type. Draw a card for each creature you control of that type" — name Elf, usually 4–6 cards. A 6-mana flier, so a bench-level add.

Jin-Gitaxias, Progress Tyrant.text: Copies your first artifact/instant/sorcery each turn — a second Traumatize empties a library — and counters the opponent's first one. Mana value 7, so Glarb casts it off the top.

The Magic Mirror.text: `{6}{U}{U}{U}` and wants instants/sorceries in the yard.

Wan Shi Tong, Librarian.text: Owned. Flash X body that draws half X, and more when they search; decent filler.

Gadwick, the Wizened.text: Draw X for `{X}{U}{U}{U}` — triple blue in a three-colour deck.

Aphelia, Viper Whisperer.text: An attack-for-value 2-drop; neither deck is an attacking deck.

Reezug, the Bonecobbler.text: Casts a creature card from the yard as an artifact; recasting an Elf takes its ability off Thranduil.

Splinter, the Mentor.text: Its partner text does nothing in Brawl.

Azula, Ruthless Firebender.text: A discard-on-attack outlet; Thranduil already loots, Glarb rarely attacks.

Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor.text: Combat draws; its `{4}{B}{B}{B}` exile needs a hand to discard.

Isareth the Awakener.text: Reanimates on attack for {X}, but the returned creature is exiled if it leaves — and the reanimated Elf no longer lends Thranduil its ability.

Kaervek, the Punisher.text: "exile up to one target black card from your graveyard and copy it" — Needs crimes; few black cards to copy outside the Elf core.

Yahenni, Undying Partisan.text: A sac outlet with nothing to sacrifice for value.

Davriel, Soul Broker.text: **Thranduil:** −3 perpetual −3/−3; +1 taxes attackers. Real removal the classifier misses. **Glarb:** Same.

Doctor Doom, Unrivaled.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** `{T}: draw a card` on a 4-mana lifelink body — fine; non-Elf.

Erebos, God of the Dead.text: **Thranduil:** `{1}{B}, Pay 2 life: Draw a card`. **Glarb:** Same, and each draw mills two.

Gisa, Glorious Resurrector.text: Steals THEIR dead creatures for a turn; off-plan here (a better fit for a removal-heavy deck).

Kels, Fight Fixer.text: Sacrifice payoff; the deck has no sacrifice engine (Yawgmoth would be the outlet, see A).

Liliana of the Dark Realms.text: Counts Swamps; three-colour decks run few.

Lo and Li, Royal Advisors.text: `{2}{U/B}: Target player mills four cards`, repeatable at instant speed; an Advisor (with Bruvac and The Master of Lake-town) that grows when they mill.

Madame Hydra, Reanimated.text: Self-mill 2 per attack and grows with creature cards; a non-Elf 4-drop beater in a deck whose bodies want to be Elves.

Massacre Girl, Known Killer.text: Wither plus draw — good against go-wide, off-plan for both.

Moonstone, Harsh Mistress.text: Not an Elf — "Whenever you discard a card, you may exile that card … you may play that card" — every Thranduil loot becomes card-neutral. But it EXILES the discard, which removes an Elf's ability from Thranduil (G-42), so it is best with non-Elf discards. ◇

One Ring to Rule Them All.text: **Thranduil:** Chapter II "Destroy all nonlegendary creatures" kills most of the Elves. **Glarb:** II is nearly one-sided here (6 nonlegendary creatures), I mills each player by your Ring-bearer's power, and III drains for each creature card in THEIR graveyard — which the mill fills. **Strong add.**

Rev, Tithe Extractor.text: Treasure + steal on combat damage — same problem.

Yawgmoth, Thran Physician.text: Not an Elf; the deck runs no dedicated sacrifice outlet — `Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: -1/-1 counter … and draw a card` is repeatable removal plus card draw off the Elf tokens (Imperious Perfect, Elvish Warmaster, Voice of the Woods, Lathril).

Whisper, Blood Liturgist.text: Sacrifice two to reanimate — costly without tokens.

Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of.text: A 5-mana flier with hand attack; strong card, no Elf or graveyard tie.

Ashiok, Wicked Manipulator.text: "If you would pay life … exile that many cards from the top of your library instead" — Phyrexian Arena, Doctor Doom and Infernal Grasp would exile YOUR library in a deck that already draws hard. Its −7 is a real finisher; the static is the problem.

Black Widow, Daring Operative.text: Mill 3 then drains = creature cards in yard on combat damage — combat-gated, 5 mana.

Drana, the Last Bloodchief.text: "defending player chooses a nonlegendary creature card" — the OPPONENT picks, so they give you a mana Elf.

Garruk, Veiled Butcher.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** Interaction (+2 shrink, −2 edict) and −3 card advantage; the deck's interaction is already 16.

Ghoulcaller Gisa.text: Sac outlet that makes Zombies = power; Elves are small, so X is 1–2.

Gisa, the Hellraiser.text: **Thranduil:** Zombies on crimes (any removal you aim at them) — off-tribe. **Glarb:** Same.

Junji, the Midnight Sky.text: A 5-mana flier whose value is its death trigger; the deck wants Elves in the yard, not Dragons.

Lo and Li, Twin Tutors.text: Tutors a Noble: Thranduil's deck has Elrond, Moon-Reader and Maralen, Glarb's has Princess Yue. Thin targets.

Maha, Its Feathers Night.text: **Thranduil:** Their creatures have base toughness 1 — pairs with Gloom Ripper. Flier. **Glarb:** A big flier.

Sauron, the Necromancer.text: "Whenever Sauron attacks, exile target creature card from your graveyard" — Same tax each attack; the token is temporary.

Seizan, Perverter of Truth.text: "At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player loses 2 life and draws two cards": the opponent loses two library cards a turn, and your two draws mill four through Psychic Corrosion. Symmetric, which this deck wants (it already runs Dictate of Kruphix).

Seymour Flux.text: Pay 1 life: draw one each upkeep — a Phyrexian Arena on a body, and Arena is in.

Shredder, Shadow Master.text: A combat finisher with no synergy.

Syr Konrad, the Grim.text: Pings on every creature death, mill and leave-graveyard; strong in a self-mill deck, but 5 mana for 1-point pings. Bench.

Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lant.text: Needs the opponent to sacrifice or discard; neither deck forces it often.

Witch-king of Angmar.text: A defensive edict against attackers; Ring tempt unused.

Doctor Doom.text: **Thranduil:** Two 3/3 Doombots and a draw each end step for 6. **Glarb:** The end-step draw mills two.

Bolas's Citadel.text: Glarb already casts MV 4+ off the top; Citadel adds the cheap ones for life. `{3}{B}{B}{B}` with 20 black sources, and the life matters against aggro.

Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni.text: Reanimates THEIR creature on combat damage — both decks rarely connect.

Lich's Mastery.text: Losing life exiles your own permanents; too risky in both.

The Cloning of Shredder.text: "Exile target creature card from your graveyard" — Six mana for copies of a card Thranduil was already using.

Vraska, Betrayal's Sting.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** 0: draw (mills two) and proliferate; −2 neutralises a creature. A fine add; 6 mana.

K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth.text: Life-for-mana with no black-pip payoff worth it.

Morlun, Devourer of Spiders.text: An X-cost beater; its drain hits only opponents.

Celeborn the Wise.text: "Whenever you attack with one or more Elves, scry 1" and a pump — combat-only, minor.

Leyline Immersion.text: **Thranduil:** On Thranduil: ward 2 and `{T}`: five mana for spells — but it spends the {T} he uses for borrowed abilities. **Glarb:** Same on Glarb: it spends his surveil tap.

Mythweaver Poq.text: Land ramp off a narrow trigger.

Radagast of Rhosgobel.text: First creature each turn costs {2} less with flash; 20 creatures, few of them cheap.

Tyvar Kell.text: Missed by the pile pass (graded for the old graveyard plan). "Elves you control have `{T}: Add {B}`" fixes black on all 11 mana Elves, 0 makes an Elf every turn, +1 untaps one, and the −6 emblem draws two per Elf spell. **Strong add.**

Ashaya, Soul of the Wild.text: Makes your creatures lands — no landfall payoff to cash it in.

Bosco, Just a Bear.text: Food with no Food payoff in either deck.

Greensleeves, Maro-Sorcerer.text: Landfall threat; neither deck plays extra lands often.

Wrenn and Seven.text: Not an Elf; Wrenn and Realmbreaker took the green-walker slot — +1 reveals four, lands to hand and "the rest into your graveyard" — a self-mill that never misses a land drop; −3 is a huge reach body. A real upgrade for any non-Elf slot.

Garruk, Caller of Beasts.text: **Thranduil:** +1: reveal five, all creature cards to hand — about 2 a turn with 45 creatures in 99 cards. A real card-advantage engine for the Elf deck. **Glarb:** 20 creatures, so +1 finds about one.

Invasion of Ikoria // Zilortha, Apex of.text: Not an Elf; competes with Kamahl's Druidic Vow and Journey as a cheat — `search your library and/or graveyard for a non-Human creature card with mana value X or less and put it onto the battlefield` — a tutor that also reanimates; finds Priest of Titania at X=2.

Golbez, Crystal Collector.text: Needs artifacts; neither deck has many.

Lazav, the Multifarious.text: Copies a creature card in the yard for {X} — mostly copying an Elf Thranduil already has.

The Ancient One.text: Loot that mills a player; descend 8 to attack; non-Elf.

Zimone the Calculating // Simple Subtrac.text: Prepared on self-mill; the adventure is a −3/−0. Minor.

Lazav, Familiar Stranger.text: Can exile your own yard — a cost in Thranduil's deck; little in Glarb's.

Ringsight.text: **Thranduil:** Tutor a card sharing a colour with a legendary creature. **Glarb:** Same.

Rona, Disciple of Gix.text: Exiles one of YOUR historic cards to cast later and exiles your own top card for {4}; little here.

Emet-Selch of the Third Seat.text: Pays off instants/sorceries from the yard; the deck runs 8.

Phenax, God of Deception.text: Gives your creatures `{T}: Target player mills X cards, where X is this creature's toughness`. Most of the 20 creatures here have toughness 4–5 (Bruvac, Matoya, Reed, both Sheoldreds, Silumgar, M.O.D.O.K.), so each is a mill-4 engine, doubled under Bruvac. Indestructible.

Uchbenbak, the Great Mistake.text: Descend 8 recursion for a 6/4 vigilance-menace body; nothing Elf.

Ultimecia, Time Sorceress.text: Transform: "exile eight cards from your graveyard" — Eight cards is most of Thranduil's toolbox; the extra turn costs nine mana.

Ashiok, Sculptor of Fears.text: In Glarb's list. **Why not Thranduil's:** +2 draws and mills BOTH players two — your two feed Thranduil; −5 reanimates from any yard. **Good add here too.**

Krang & Shredder.text: Owned. Exiles to a nonland and casts it if a permanent left your control — needs a sacrifice the deck lacks.

Xanathar, Guild Kingpin.text: Strong — they cannot cast spells on your turn and you play their top card — but 6 mana for a value engine the mill plan does not need. Bench.

Prototype X-8.text: 10 mana minus 2 per creature card in the yard; its "sacrifice it, conjure a duplicate" line is a gimmick here.

Chevill, Bane of Monsters.text: Bounty card advantage needs repeat removal to cash in.

Slimefoot, Thallid Transplant.text: Card advantage off basics entering; few basics, no Fungus plan.

Vraska Joins Up.text: **Thranduil:** Deathtouch counters; draw when a legend deals combat damage — the Elves do attack. **Glarb:** Rarely attacks.

Dina, Essence Brewer.text: Sacrifice payoff; neither deck has a sacrifice outlet.

Long Feng, Grand Secretariat.text: Counters payoff; neither deck stacks counters.

Pharika, God of Affliction.text: Exiles creature cards from graveyards — fights Thranduil's yard; gives the card's owner a token.

Sméagol, Helpful Guide.text: Needs a creature to die each turn for the Ring to tempt you.

Furgul, Quag Nurturer.text: `{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {G}` equal to power — a sac outlet Thranduil can borrow, plus a free Leech each turn. The closest of these to a swap; Alchemy (conjure). ◇

Nissa of Shadowed Boughs.text: −5 reanimates; landfall loyalty — the deck plays ~1 land a turn, so −5 is slow.

Nemata, Primeval Warden.text: Exiles their dying creatures (keeps them out of the graveyard Consuming Aberration counts) and draws off Saprolings.

Tyvar the Bellicose.text: Missed at draft time — Legendary Elf; "Whenever a mana ability of this creature resolves, put +1/+1 counters equal to the mana produced" turns the 11 mana Elves into growing bodies; Elves attacking gain deathtouch.

Vraska, Golgari Queen.text: In Thranduil's list. **Why not Glarb's:** +2 needs a permanent to sacrifice; −3 kills mana value 3 or less. Fine.

Beledros Witherbloom.text: Pest each upkeep; 7 mana and "Pay 10 life" untap — no Elf payoff for Pests.

Arwen Undómiel.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf (a loot trigger), but its payoff is scry, which the deck barely does. **Glarb:** Scry payoff with Matoya; small.

Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy.text: Missed by the pile pass. "Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana of any type that permanent produced" doubles all 11 mana Elves, and `{5}{G}{U}` puts a non-Human creature (any Elf) from the top five onto the battlefield. **Strong add.**

Absorbing Man.text: A gimmick with no tie to either engine.

Albiorix, Goose Tyrant // Wild Goose Cha.text: **Thranduil:** The adventure draws two, discards two — fuel. Flier body after. **Glarb:** Draw two mills four.

Galadriel of Lothlórien.text: **Thranduil:** Legendary Elf; scry ramp needs the Ring. **Glarb:** Lands onto the battlefield on scry — ramp plus Matoya draws.

Kiora of Salt and Sand.text: Superfriends support; neither deck runs enough walkers.

Kasmina, Enigma Sage.text: +2 scry 1 (feeds Matoya) and shares loyalty abilities with the deck's three Ashioks and Jaces — cute, low impact.

Nissa, Steward of Elements.text: Scry 2 and puts lands/small creatures from the top into play; green-blue value without a mill tie.

Drowned Secrets.text: "Whenever you cast a blue spell, target player mills two cards" — 42 blue spells here. A 2-mana engine that does not need a draw.

Navigator's Ruin.text: Raid — mill four only if you attacked; this deck rarely attacks.

Fleet Swallower.text: "Whenever this creature attacks, target player mills half their library" — a 7-mana creature that must attack; Traumatize and kicked Maddening Cacophony do it from the hand.

Ashiok, Dream Render.text: Cut at draft: its −1 "exile each opponent's graveyard" empties the yard Consuming Aberration, Drown in the Loch and Sheoldred's transform count.

Cut Your Losses.text: Half a library for 6 (twice with casualty); the deck already holds Traumatize, Maddening Cacophony and Jidoor's Overture as half-library mills.

Altar of Dementia.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Altar of Dementia.text: "Sacrifice a creature: mills … equal to the sacrificed creature's power" — the deck makes almost no fodder (its tokens are a few Ashiok Nightmares).

Grindstone.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Grindstone.text: `{3}, {T}`: mill two, repeating while the two share a colour — about 2–4 a turn for 3 mana each turn.

Villainous Wealth.text: Exile X of their library and cast them — real library exile, but `{X}{B}{G}{U}` competes with Tasha's Hideous Laughter, which exiles until 20 total mana value — usually ten or more cards — for 3.

Mind's Dilation.text: 7 mana; exiles one card per opponent spell — slow as library exile.

Visions of Beyond.text: 1 mana: "If a graveyard has twenty or more cards in it, draw three cards instead" — the opponent's graveyard passes 20 early here, so it is a 1-mana draw-three (six milled through Corrosion).

Folio of Fancies.text: `{X}{X}, {T}`: each player draws X (both libraries shrink; yours mills them twice through Corrosion), then `{2}{U}` mills them equal to hand size. A real engine; bench.

Lord of the Forsaken.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Lord of the Forsaken.text: `{B}, Sacrifice another creature: mill three` — same missing fodder; 6 mana.

Persistent Petitioners.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Persistent Petitioners.text: Its 12-card mill needs four Advisors tapped; it is the one card a deck may run in any number, so it only works as a dozen-copy package — a different deck.

Cruel Somnophage // Can't Wake Up.text: Mill four for 2, then a body that grows with creature cards in all graveyards. Fine; smaller than the deck's 2-mana mills (Glimpse the Unthinkable mills ten).

Gyruda, Doom of Depths.text: "Each player mills four cards" and you take a creature from among them — a one-shot, symmetric 6-drop.

Duskmantle, House of Shadow.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Duskmantle, House of Shadow.text: A land that makes only colourless — in a three-colour deck already at 3.5 points of tapped-land cost — for a 3-mana mill one.

Hama, the Bloodbender.text: Owned. Mills three and lets you cast one of their noncreature spells by waterbending — deck 22's engine piece; a 5-mana one-shot here.

Didn't Say Please.text: Counter + mill three — the same card as Thought Collapse, which is in. The first card to add if you want more counters.

Bloodchief's Thirst.text: **Thranduil:** Sorcery; 1 mana early, 4 kicked for anything. Interchangeable. **Glarb:** Same.

Keening Stone.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Keening Stone.text: 6 to cast and `{5}, {T}` to mill X = their graveyard; Riverchurn Monument's exhaust does the same once for 4.

Riverchurn Monument.text: Owned. `{1}, {T}`: mill two every turn, and once per game its exhaust mills "cards equal to the number of cards in their graveyard" — doubles a half-milled yard.

Terisian Mindbreaker.text: Half a library on attack, unearth for `{1}{U}{U}{U}`; a 7-mana artifact creature doing Fleet Swallower's job.

Scavenger's Talent.text: Same — Food and "whenever you sacrifice" need an outlet the deck lacks.

Brain Freeze.text: Mill three plus storm; the deck casts one or two spells a turn, so it is usually mill three.

Jin-Gitaxias // The Great Synthesis.text: "Whenever you cast a noncreature spell with mana value 3 or greater, draw a card" — 28 such spells here, and each draw mills two. Owned. Lost its slot to Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur, but both fit.

Howling Mine.text: Symmetric extra draw — the same job as Dictate of Kruphix, which is in; a second one would refill their hand too. Bench.

Hullbreaker Horror.text: A 7-mana bounce engine; strong in control, but each turn's mill matters more than tempo here.

Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student // Tamiyo, S.text: **Thranduil:** Flips on the third draw in a turn — Thranduil's loot gets there; the walker's −3 regrows instants/sorceries (8 here). **Glarb:** Flips on your third draw — routine here — and her −7 draws half your library: through Psychic Corrosion that mills them for about twice as many. Spicy, risky.

Kenrith's Transformation.text: **Thranduil:** Turns a threat into a 3/3 and draws a card. **Glarb:** Same, and the draw mills two.

Toxic Deluge.text: **Thranduil:** A sweeper that kills your own Elves. **Glarb:** A sweeper; the deck already runs Damnation.

Murderous Rider // Swift End.text: **Thranduil:** Instant kill + a lifelink body. Interchangeable with Go for the Throat. **Glarb:** Same.

Saw It Coming.text: **Thranduil:** Off-plan here. **Glarb:** A 3-mana counter (foretell 2); outranked by Wizard's Retort.

Memory Lapse.text: **Thranduil:** Counters are off-plan in a tap-out Elf deck. **Glarb:** Counter that puts the spell back on top of their library — it delays, and it undoes a mill.

Feed the Swarm.text: **Thranduil:** Also kills an enchantment — one of the few noncreature answers; you lose life equal to its mana value. **Glarb:** Same.

Tear Asunder.text: **Thranduil:** Kicked, it exiles any nonland permanent — the deck answers few noncreature permanents (4 of 15 pieces). Good add. **Glarb:** Same: kicked, a 4-mana exile-anything; the deck has Assassin's Trophy and Cyclonic Rift already.

Anoint with Affliction.text: **Thranduil:** Mana value 3 or less only. **Glarb:** Same.

Fatal Push.text: **Thranduil:** Mana value 2 or less without revolt — narrow in Brawl's bigger threats. **Glarb:** Same.

Bitter Triumph.text: **Thranduil:** Discard a card — fuel here — or pay 3 life: instant kill of a creature or planeswalker. Good fit. **Glarb:** Discarding costs a card in a draw deck; pay 3 life instead.

Sheoldred's Edict.text: **Thranduil:** Instant edict that also hits planeswalkers or a token. Interchangeable. **Glarb:** Same.

Mystic Snake.text: **Thranduil:** Off-plan here. **Glarb:** Flash counter on a body; `{1}{G}{U}{U}` on 15 green sources.

Pongify.text: **Thranduil:** 1 mana but gives them a 3/3. **Glarb:** Same.

Talisman of Resilience.text: **Thranduil:** Elves are better ramp here. **Glarb:** Cut at draft for Kaito, Bane of Nightmares.

Cultivate.text: **Thranduil:** Two basics; the deck ramps on Elves. **Glarb:** Slower than the rocks in the list.

Nature's Lore.text: **Thranduil:** Fetches any Forest-typed land untapped — Overgrown Tomb, Breeding Pool, Zagoth Triome. The deck already has 11 mana Elves. **Glarb:** Same; 8 ramp pieces already.

Farseek.text: **Thranduil:** Finds Watery Grave / Overgrown Tomb tapped. Fine. **Glarb:** Same.

Delighted Halfling.text: **Thranduil:** Any colour for legendary spells, uncounterable — good with 17 legendary Elves, but not an Elf. **Glarb:** Fewer legends here.

Thought Scour.text: **Thranduil:** Target yourself: mill two, draw one. **Glarb:** Cut at draft for Theorix Charm; target them: mill two, and the draw mills two more.

Opt.text: Scry 1 then draw — under Matoya that is two draws, four milled. A cheap filler; Brainstorm is in.

Preordain.text: Scry 2 then draw; same as Opt, slightly better.

Consider.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 1 + draw. **Glarb:** Surveil triggers Matoya: two draws for 1 mana.

Memory Deluge.text: Instant: two of the top X, then flashback — four draws for eight mana of the late game, each draw milling two.

The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools.text: **Thranduil:** Mill two, draw two — the mill feeds Thranduil. **Glarb:** Draw two mills four through Corrosion. Owned. Either is fine.

Sokka's Haiku.text: Owned. Counter + draw, but "mill three cards" mills YOU, and it costs 5.

Arcane Epiphany.text: Draw three for 4 (Glarb is a Wizard); fine, outranked by the repeatable engines.

Laboratory Maniac.text: Self-mill alt-win; a 100-card deck never empties its own library on purpose.

Rot Farm Mortipede.text: +1/+1 counters or menace/lifelink when cards leave — Vanilla-ish bodies that need the event every turn.

Wizard's Retort.text: **Thranduil:** No Wizards; a plain 3-mana counter. **Glarb:** Glarb is a Frog Wizard, so it costs `{U}{U}` with Glarb out. The best counter left out.

Desecrated Tomb.text: "…leave your graveyard, create a 1/1 black Bat" — Weaker Chalk Outline.

Chalk Outline.text: "Whenever one or more creature cards leave your graveyard, create a 2/2 … then investigate" — Best of the rest; 4-mana do-nothing until a recast. First reserve if the recursion count grows.

Attuned Hunter.text: +1/+1 counters or menace/lifelink when cards leave — Vanilla-ish bodies that need the event every turn.

Kishla Skimmer.text: "Whenever a card leaves your graveyard during your turn, draw a card" (once a turn) — Fine card draw, but a 2-mana non-Elf; Elrond, Moon-Reader is the draw engine here.

Undead Hand Ninja.text: drain 1 when creature cards leave — Too small.

Dredger's Insight.text: ETB mill four, take an artifact/creature/land — A one-shot dig; the deck has better self-mill on Elf bodies.

Along the Crooked Way.text: ETB "return target creature card … to your hand"; leave → amass Goblins — The Goblin army is off-tribe.

Willow Geist.text: +1/+1 counters or menace/lifelink when cards leave — Vanilla-ish bodies that need the event every turn.

Courser of Kruphix.text: Lands from the top plus life; Glarb does the first part. `{1}{G}{G}` on 15 green sources.

Augur of Autumn.text: Lands from the top — Glarb does it; the creature half needs coven.

Oracle of Mul Daya.text: **Thranduil:** An Elf: extra land drop and lands from the top. Good. **Glarb:** Extra land drop plus Ruin Crab's landfall; Glarb already plays lands from the top.

Precognition Field.text: Instants and sorceries from the top (21 here) — the closest of these; covers the cheap ones Glarb cannot. Bench.

Vivien, Monsters' Advocate.text: Creatures from the top; the deck runs 20 creatures, mostly utility. `{3}{G}{G}`.

Eladamri, Korvecdal.text: Missed at draft time — Legendary Elf (a loot); "You may cast creature spells from the top of your library" with 45 creatures; from the yard Thranduil gets `{G}, {T}, Tap two untapped creatures: … put it onto the battlefield` — a free creature cheat every turn.

Inside Information.text: Exile X and play them this turn for life; a one-turn burst.

Deathrite Shaman.text: Missed at draft time — it surfaced in the phase-1 Elf search but never reached the list — A 1-mana Elf with THREE activated abilities, so it is a Thranduil card twice: in play, and in the yard (`{T}: Exile target land card from a graveyard. Add one mana of any color`; `{B}`: drain 2; `{G}`: gain 2). Can target the OPPONENT'S graveyard, so it need not eat Elves. **Strongest add on this list.**
